confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors come from aggregated cost-of-living figures found by web search in 2026. Expatica, using Numbeo data from June 2026, gave about EUR 18.7 for an inexpensive meal, EUR 2.1 for a cappuccino and EUR 3.4 for a 0.5 L beer. MyLifeElsewhere gave about EUR 15 for a meal, EUR 2.05 for a cappuccino and EUR 3.3 for a beer. I used a blended inexpensive meal price of about EUR 17. The mid-range meal for two is less certain. Search sources ranged from about EUR 58 to EUR 150, and most of those figures included wine. I used about EUR 70 without drinks. For wine, search results put txakoli or house wine at EUR 2 to 3.50 at bars, so I used about EUR 3.3 for a restaurant glass. Cocktail evidence was thin: one 2026 source listed a premium gin and tonic at EUR 9 to 14, so I used about EUR 9.5 for a standard cocktail. I converted euros to US dollars at about 1.10 USD per EUR. This is implied by the RBA rates for 18 Nov 2026 (0.6720 USD and 0.6115 EUR per AUD) as reported in a search result. All accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge for July, which is peak summer. They were not checked against live listings and carry the most uncertainty. The RBA rate was taken from search-result content that cites the RBA homepage fixing for 4pm on 18 Nov 2026. I did not open the RBA page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Bilbao is a mid-sized, relatively expensive Spanish city, priced above the Spanish average but somewhat below Madrid. Accommodation is benchmarked against northern Spanish cities such as San Sebastián (cheaper than Bilbao) and Santander, and against Madrid, using July high-season demand.
